# PlateFold updater dependency patch

This directory carries tauri-plugin-updater 2.11.0 from crates.io under its original MIT or Apache-2.0 licenses. PlateFold uses its native installer and artifact signature verification. The release archive and file hashes are recorded in `UPSTREAM.json`.

The upstream public API always fetches release metadata during `check()`. PlateFold has already bounded and authenticated that metadata. Calling `check()` again would let a changing server send an unbounded second response. `check_from_json()` constructs the same native update from the verified release fields without another request. Both paths share version/target selection and retain the configured timeout.

`download_bounded()` checks the advertised length and every chunk before extending its buffer. PlateFold supplies the signed artifact size and permits at most two HTTPS redirects, only to GitHub's release-asset hosts. Metadata requests still refuse redirects. Signature verification runs after download. The existing `download()` API remains available for upstream compatibility; PlateFold does not call it.

Upstream replaces a macOS app by moving it into an automatically deleted temporary folder; if the new app then fails to move in, the error return deletes that folder and the only remaining copy. Its administrator-assisted path deletes the installed app before moving the new one, and quotes paths so that one containing a quote breaks the command. The AppImage path also keeps its backup in an automatically deleted folder, which a failed restore would delete. PlateFold replaces both through `src/updater/replace.rs`, staging the new copy beside the installed one. An AppImage is replaced by one rename onto the installed file. A macOS app is exchanged with the staged one in a single `renamex_np(RENAME_SWAP)` call, and the previous copy is then deleted from the staging folder. Either way, the installed path holds the previous or the new copy at every moment, so an exit at any point during the replacement still leaves an app to launch. On a macOS volume that cannot exchange two names, such as HFS+, the updater refuses with `Error::ReplacementUnsupported`: nothing is moved, and the app is updated by hand. The updater explicitly attempts to delete the staging folder after the installation attempt. If cleanup fails after a refused exchange, the error names the unused staging folder so the user can delete it. If it fails after any other result, that result stands and the folder is recorded in the `CleanupReport` passed to `Update::cleanup_report`, which PlateFold adds to its Updates warning. Cleanup may already have deleted some of its contents.

`CommitGate` (`src/updater/gate.rs`) guards replacement of the installed app and the Windows installer launch. A close during installation normally waits for the attempt's result. After 60 seconds from the close request, PlateFold abandons further replacement and closes once the gate is idle. If replacement or installer launch is already running, it waits for that step, so 60 seconds is not a hard closing deadline. `Update::restart_cancelled_by` lets a close withdraw a requested Windows restart before the restart flag is read while preparing the installer launch.

Upstream's administrator-assisted macOS path is removed, with its `osakit` dependency. It extracted the verified app into the user's temporary folder and asked an administrator to move that folder into place, so any process running as that user could change the app while the password prompt was open. A macOS app in a folder the account can't change now fails before anything moves, and PlateFold shows manual update steps before offering a download, as it does for a root-owned AppImage.

`src/updater.rs` and `src/error.rs` differ from the copied upstream files, `src/updater/replace.rs`, `src/updater/gate.rs`, `src/updater/cleanup.rs` and the replacement tests are added, and `Cargo.toml` adds test dependencies and drops the macOS `osakit` dependency. The added tests cover construction without a reachable metadata endpoint, signatures (including a rewritten trusted comment, which PlateFold uses to bind each artifact to its release), redirects, declared and streamed oversize bodies, and interrupted transfer. The replacement tests use real directories to check the AppImage rename, the emulated macOS exchange and failures at each filesystem step. They also check that a refused exchange leaves the installed bundle unchanged. They never install a package. They emulate the macOS exchange, because `renamex_np` exists only on macOS, and the macOS code itself is not compiled on Linux; `cargo clippy -p tauri-plugin-updater --target aarch64-apple-darwin --no-default-features --features native-tls` type-checks it after `rustup target add aarch64-apple-darwin`.

Run from `desktop/src-tauri`:

```console
cargo test --locked --workspace --no-default-features --features tauri-plugin-updater/rustls-tls
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo check --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
```

When upgrading, compare the changed files against the recorded upstream version, retain both licenses, and rerun the workspace tests and native installer qualification. Remove the local patch only when the replacement preserves authenticated metadata reuse, transport bounds, timeout propagation, signature verification, and a replacement that keeps the previous app until the new one is in place.

## TLS validation

The vendored client always keeps TLS certificate and hostname validation enabled for metadata requests and installer downloads. Configuration deserialization rejects either dangerous validation-bypass option when true, including its kebab-case alias. The client contains no branch that disables either check. Native release tests use an explicitly trusted test certificate rather than disabling verification.
